analysis.title: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
key_insights: Core PCE was 3.0% year over year in August 2026, 0.7pp above GS's 2.3% start-of-the-year forecast for August. GS decomposes the surprise by category and driver to test whether it reflects one-offs or broader stickiness.
Computer software and accessories plus other electronics account for more than 0.3pp of the overshoot, reflecting a larger-than-expected AI-related boost to consumer prices.

Computer software and accessories alone contributes 0.2pp. GS estimates the component overstates the underlying price impulse by 0.1pp because its PCE weight is roughly 30 times its CPI weight and it is not quality-adjusted like other technology components.
The PCE source data overstates software sales to retail customers, so the PCE computer and accessories component has diverged significantly from its CPI analogue (Exhibit 2).
GS expects the software and accessories contribution to ease in 2027 as the memory price shock fades.

Air transportation accounts for 0.2pp of the surprise, largely from higher jet fuel prices tied to the war with Iran. Energy cost passthrough to air transportation and other components totals 0.3pp of the surprise.

Other core goods contributed 0.1pp, roughly a third of it from greater-than-expected tariff passthrough. GS raised its peak consumer tariff passthrough estimate to 80% from 70% in January, largely offset by a lower effective tariff rate after the Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariffs. The tariff surprise is 0.1pp across core goods.
Shelter added roughly 0.1pp to the upside surprise because it slowed by less than expected. GS still expects further shelter disinflation in coming months.

Pharmaceuticals and used vehicles subtracted a combined 0.2pp versus forecast, which GS sees as durable price level changes unlikely to reverse. Pharma reflects Medicare drug price negotiation, the TrumpRx discount program and patent expirations. Used vehicles reflect an unwind of H2 2025 increases and cooling demand from higher interest rates.
Roughly three-fourths of the surprise comes from the oil shock, tariffs and the software and accessories component (overstatement plus memory prices), which GS expects to ease over the next year.

About 0.2pp is genuine upside, mostly from housing and other AI-exposed electronics. GS sees no evidence of a meaningful acceleration in underlying inflation versus its start-of-year forecast and still forecasts core PCE falling to 2.2% by December 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: 0.7pp above GS's 2.3% start-of-year forecast. GS attributes about three-fourths of the overshoot to one-time factors and mismeasurement.

macro_indicators.indicator: Core PCE inflation, GS start-of-year forecast for August
macro_indicators.interpretation: The benchmark against which the 0.7pp surprise is measured.
GS bottom-up model (Exhibit 5) shows a slight decline from the August reading.
Gradual disinflation as temporary factors fade, leaving core PCE near target.

macro_indicators.indicator: Peak consumer tariff passthrough, GS model
macro_indicators.interpretation: Raised from 70% assumed in January, but largely offset by a lower effective tariff rate after the IEEPA ruling.

risk_factors: Underlying stickiness could keep inflation higher for longer if the overshoot is not one-off.
Genuine upside of about 0.2pp from housing and other AI-exposed electronics.
Shelter disinflation has been slower than GS assumed.
Energy cost passthrough from the Iran war oil shock.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows the August year-over-year core PCE surprise by component, split into oil-driven, tariff-driven and residual parts, with software and accessories and air transport the largest positive contributors and pharma and used vehicles negative.

Exhibit 5 shows GS's bottom-up core PCE model: August 2026 core PCE 3.0% year over year, 2.9% in December 2026 and 2.2% in December 2027. Air transportation is 19.4% year over year in August, falling to 16.7% by December 2026 and -2.3% by December 2027. Video, audio and computers is 10.5% in August.
geopolitical: War with Iran has raised jet fuel prices, feeding air transportation inflation.
Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariffs lowered the effective tariff rate.

tension_points.bull_case: About three-fourths of the 0.7pp overshoot comes from the oil shock, tariffs and the software and accessories component (overstatement and memory prices), which should fade. Core PCE falls to 2.2% by December 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: About 0.2pp of genuine upside remains, mostly from housing and AI-exposed electronics, and shelter disinflation has been slower than assumed. Pharma and used vehicle declines that offset the surprise are durable and will not reverse.

theme_stances.key_argument: Most of the core PCE surprise comes from one-time factors and mismeasurement that should fade, so underlying inflation has not meaningfully accelerated.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not see strong evidence of a significant acceleration in the underlying trend of inflation
